rule: mixed: the rule is fireable, but 'Sunken-Cove tending' is read as tending the Cove itself — the Cove becomes the thing being tended — where your other sentences make it tending done at the Cove. Put the place in a plain prepositional phrase: "Large feather stores enable safe tending at the Sunken Cove."
texts: good. one fireable rule keyed on the store being large, with the Keepers, the Sunken Cove lanterns, 'safely' and 'in winter' all carried, and the lanterns linked to the Cove rather than renamed after it.

bad: the rule can never fire, because its condition names a holding event that is asserted nowhere; worse, the large feather store from the 'if' clause is also recorded as a standing fact, so the knowledge base ends up claiming the Watch really does hold a large store when the sentence only supposes it. Word the condition as a plain state of the store, exactly as your 'when' version does: "When the feather store at the Watch is large, winter tending at the Sunken Cove stays safe."
good. the issuing, the feather rations, the Sunken-Cove station as the recipient and the winter timing are all carried, with the station linked to the named Cove rather than renamed after it.
good. a fireable rule keyed on the feather store being small, with the growing wraith risk as its consequence and nothing asserted beyond the words.
